resources.string: The right time for every task
Kairos 3 is being rewritten. This screen arrives in an upcoming preview; version 2 remains the everyday tool until then.
What Kairos does, the priority score, the version
Kairos ranks your tasks for the day and fits them into the gaps of your calendar, at the right time.
It ranks the day’s tasks by a priority score, shown on each one.
It fits each task into the gaps of the calendar, around meetings, with a buffer after each meeting.
It protects deep-work blocks and lightens the afternoon slump.
It tracks the time actually spent and compares it with the estimate.

Value grows fourfold with each priority step (P0 is worth 4 times P1), the deadline weighs more and more as it approaches, and effort is measured in Fibonacci points. Small and important goes before big and distant. An overdue task always goes first.
In Greek, kairos means the opportune moment, the right instant to act, as opposed to chronos, time passing by. That is the tool’s job: finding the right slot for each task.
